summary: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships are jointly funded by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission and UK universities for students from lower-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK. They fund selected one-year master's courses.
meta_description: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027–28: apply from 10 November to 8 December 2026 for a UK master's with fees, flights and £1,712 a month.
covers: Approved return airfare between your home country and the UK.
A monthly stipend of £1,712, or £2,000 at universities in the London metropolitan area (current rates).
Thesis and study travel grants and a warm clothing allowance where they apply, and a child allowance for widowed, divorced or single-parent scholars (£622 a month for the first child).
eligibility: Citizens of one of the 43 eligible Commonwealth countries, including Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, India and Bangladesh.
Proof that you cannot afford to study in the UK without the scholarship.
No more than one academic year of study or work in a high-income country.
A 2:1 first degree, or a 2:2 plus a relevant postgraduate qualification, by September 2027, and able to start in the UK that month. There is no age limit.
how_to_apply: Find the participating UK universities and their approved master's courses; the CSC publishes the 2027 list before applications open.
Apply for admission to your chosen course at the university and secure a place.
Apply for the scholarship on CSC Central between Tuesday 10 November 2026 and 16:00 GMT on Tuesday 8 December 2026. The CSC accepts no applications or documents sent any other way.

Each university runs its own selection and nominates its chosen candidates to the CSC. If you are selected, the university tells you, and the CSC confirms the award once your admission is agreed and your health form is in.
watch_out: Only approved courses are eligible, and the 2027 list can differ from 2026's, so check it when it is published.
The financial-need test is central; explain clearly why you cannot study in the UK without it.
The window is only four weeks, so have your references and transcripts ready before 10 November.

costs: Covered in full, by agreement between the CSC and your university
Return airfare between home and the UK
Monthly stipend (£1,712, or £2,000 in London), plus thesis, warm-clothing and study-travel grants where they apply
You, as the scholarship does not cover it
You, as dependants' travel is not covered
documents: Passport or national ID showing your photo, date of birth and citizenship
Full transcripts of all your higher education, including courses in progress, with certified translations if not in English
At least two signed references as PDFs, on institutional letterhead or with an email showing the sender's details
A clear case that you could not afford to study in the UK without the scholarship
Your application to the university for the eligible master's course, by its deadline

faq.a: On CSC Central from Tuesday 10 November 2026 until 16:00 GMT on Tuesday 8 December 2026, for master's courses starting in September 2027. You must also apply for admission to the course at the university.

faq.q: I have studied abroad before. Can I still apply?
faq.a: Only if you have not studied or worked for more than one academic year in a high-income country. The scheme is for people who have not had that opportunity.
No. The Commonwealth Shared Scholarships have no age limit.

43 lower-income Commonwealth countries, including Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. Check the CSC page for the full list each year.
